correctness.rationale: For connected bipartite G, each edge-root constraint in the polar Q is |y_i|+|y_j|<=1, rendering ±e_i redundant. In every orthant the nonnegative edge-incidence inequalities have totally unimodular matrix and integral right sides, giving 0/1 independent-set vertices; the full polar vertices are exactly all signings of inclusion-maximal independent sets. Central symmetry makes maximal Euclidean inradius 1/max||q||=1/sqrt(alpha(G)). The optimal center support inequalities are sum_{i in I}|c_i|<=1-sqrt(|I|/alpha), and the active constraints from maximum sets force c_i=0 on U(G), leaving a relative full neighborhood on its complement; hence affdim=n-|U|. For odd P_{2k+1}, the unique maximum independent set is the odd positions and the center set is the k-dimensional even-coordinate l1 ball of radius 1-sqrt(k/(k+1)); for even paths, both parity classes cover V, making center unique. The tree bound floor((n-1)/2) follows by bipartition and is attained by odd paths or the specified even-order leaf attachment. Independent enumeration of all independent sets on P_n, n=2..8, reproduced alpha and center dimensions 0,k alternately. The proof is universal; enumeration is corroborative.

originality.rationale: Bipartite total unimodularity and the stable-set interpretation of the polar are classical and credited. The new final claim is the exact Euclidean inball radius, complete center polytope, affine-dimension formula, and sharp tree extremum in the canonical type-B root realization. Ohsugi--Tsuchiya investigate reflexivity, h-star and triangulations, not this Euclidean center-locus theorem in the relevant inspected sections. Similar inball theorems for type-A symmetric edge polytopes, graph associahedra, zonotopes or a graph-matching polytope cannot be transferred by name: their polar bodies and metrics are not this Q. An earlier formulation in unconditional-stable-set/antiblocking convexity remains a relevant priority risk.
